# Hardware & IoT Support

`customer_support.model.b2b.hardware_iot` · vertical · parent `customer_support.model.b2b`

> Supporting deployed physical devices — instruments, terminals, sensors, connected equipment. The structural break from every software vertical is that resolution requires atoms to move. Diagnosis may finish in twenty minutes and resolution still takes nine days, because a part has to exist in a depot, clear customs and be fitted by someone who can travel there. Time to resolve is therefore bounded by logistics rather than by expertise, and an operator who optimises agent handling time in this vertical is polishing the fast part. A workaround is not free. In software, offering a workaround costs a sentence; here it is frequently an advance replacement, which consumes a unit of inventory, ships before the faulty one comes back, and cannot be un-sent when the fault turns out to be the customer's power supply. The entitlement check that gates it is serial-number-based — warranty attaches to the unit, not to the account — so a customer with an excellent contract can still own an out-of-warranty device, and a customer with no contract can own a device still covered. Telemetry inverts the intake direction for part of the queue. We frequently know a device is failing before its owner does, which makes proactive contact possible; the same telemetry goes silent exactly when the device dies, so absence of signal is the most important signal and the easiest one to miss. The error carried in from SaaS is promising a fix on a release cadence. Firmware goes out in staged waves to fleets that cannot all be rebooted, some of which are on a boat, and rollback in the field is often not available at all.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| requester | a site engineer, facilities manager or field technician standing next to the broken thing, frequently without network access from where they are standing |
| typical_resolution_hours | 96 |
| volume_shape | steady baseline driven by installed-base size, with cohort spikes after firmware waves and after a manufacturing batch defect surfaces |
| staffing_model | tiered remote diagnosis feeding a dispatch and depot function, with field engineers scheduled against parts availability |
| coverage | business hours remote, contracted on-site response windows for covered units, on-call for safety-relevant faults |
| automation_level | moderate on diagnosis via telemetry, near zero on resolution — nothing automates a courier |
| notes | typical_resolution_hours is deliberately four days. Anything shorter describes time to diagnosis, which is the number this vertical is most often reported with and the number that misleads the most.  |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.entitlement`

Requires `expires_at`, `coverage_hours`, `entitled_channels`


> Cover here is a property of the device, and the object has to be resolvable from a serial number rather than from the account on the ticket. Every hardware support organisation has shipped a free replacement for a unit whose warranty ended two years ago because the parent account was in good standing, and every one of them has then had to explain it.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.ticket`

Requires `resolution_type`, `commitment_ref`


> Resolution type has to distinguish repair, advance replacement, RMA-return and configuration, because the four have different cost, different reversibility and different follow-up obligations. The commitment reference is mandatory because a dispatch date is a promise a person will physically wait for, and an unmet one is not recoverable with an apology email.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.sla_target`

Requires `target_type`, `calendar_type`, `exclusions`


> On-site response clocks run on business calendars with regional holidays and travel exclusions that no software SLA carries. A four-hour on-site target quoted without the calendar attached will be read by the customer as four hours from now, and they will be wrong in a way that is entirely our fault.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.incident`

Requires `affected_account_count`, `detection_source`


> Detection source matters because a batch defect is usually found by correlating telemetry across unrelated customers, not by a report. Recording that an incident was found by us rather than by a customer is what tells you whether proactive monitoring is earning its keep.
